stories.headline: IMF warns global economy is 'standing on one leg' as AI financing soars
stories.summary: The head of the International Monetary Fund, Kristalina Georgieva, isn't sugarcoating it – she says the global economy is fragile. Why? Because a huge chunk of AI investment, about $1 trillion, is "circular financing" (companies investing in each other) and two-thirds of that is debt. Sounds a bit wobbly, right?

stories.headline: UK urged to cut National Insurance to boost youth jobs
stories.summary: A new report suggests the UK needs to do more to help young people find work, including cutting National Insurance for under-25s. Apparently, it's so tough out there some parents are even offering to pay their kids' wages to get them hired. Oof.

stories.headline: Intel slapped with lawsuit over PC sales slump
stories.summary: Looks like Intel's shareholders aren't happy. The chip giant is facing a proposed class action lawsuit, with investors claiming the company kept them in the dark about how badly slowing PC sales were impacting its bottom line.

stories.headline: UK gets gas flowing from new North Sea field
stories.summary: After years of debate, the Jackdaw gas field, located off the coast of Aberdeen, has finally gotten the green light and is now supplying gas. This is a win for UK energy security, though it'll likely spark fresh debate on fossil fuel projects.

stories.headline: Employer health costs are worse than projected, hitting wallets hard
stories.summary: Brace yourselves: new data shows that double-digit increases in employer health care costs started hitting well before experts predicted. This means millions of Americans are already seeing big changes in their workplace health coverage.

stories.headline: Trump gears up for a historic summit with Xi and Putin
stories.summary: Get ready for some major global theatrics. President Trump is heading to China for a high-stakes meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Expect intense talks on everything from nuclear weapons to Middle East conflicts and even the war in Ukraine.

stories.headline: Jordan bans Telegram amid 'radicalisation' claims
stories.summary: The messaging app Telegram has been blocked in Jordan following a deadly church attack, with authorities claiming the app is a breeding ground for content that threatens "national interests." It's another move in the global chess game between governments and digital freedom.

stories.headline: ASEAN extends an olive branch (with strings attached) to Myanmar
stories.summary: Southeast Asian leaders are finally opening the door a crack for Myanmar's sidelined government. They've agreed to re-engage in stages, but only if Myanmar shows "meaningful progress" on a peace plan. Basically, come back to the table, but you gotta behave.

stories.headline: Polish activists defy strict abortion laws with "Abortomat" lockers
stories.summary: In a powerful act of resistance, Polish activists are using discreet locker systems, dubbed "Abortomats," to dispense abortion pills. This innovative, if controversial, method helps women bypass the country's incredibly restrictive abortion laws, showing how human ingenuity finds a way.

stories.headline: VHP threatens protests if Karnataka repeals controversial laws
stories.summary: The Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) is not mincing words: they've warned the Karnataka government of major protests if it moves to scrap the anti-conversion and anti-cow slaughter laws during the upcoming legislative session. Expect some heated debates.

stories.headline: Music legend Hariharan weighs in on AI's impact
stories.summary: Celebrating an incredible 50 years in music, playback singer Hariharan is sitting down to talk about his journey, the unique North-South Indian musical connection, and yes, his "AI dilemma." Even the greats are grappling with our new tech reality.

stories.headline: Italian politician's India speech stirs trouble back home
stories.summary: An Italian political leader, Deborah Bergamini, is facing criticism in her own country for a speech in India. She suggested Europeans shouldn't lecture India on democracy, given its 970 million voters. It highlights India's growing assertiveness on the global stage.

stories.headline: Youth arrested in Kochi for attempted sexual assault on elderly woman
stories.summary: A disturbing incident in Kerala where a young man was apprehended for allegedly attempting to sexually assault a 70-year-old woman who was collecting plastic waste.

stories.headline: European "moonshot" fund Plural raises a whopping $1.1 billion
stories.summary: Big news for European tech! The VC firm Plural, led by experienced operators, has just secured €1 billion (about $1.1 billion) to back the next generation of ambitious European startups. Looks like Europe is serious about building its own tech giants.

stories.headline: Amazon's satellite internet dream takes a hit as Vulcan rocket fails
stories.summary: In a major setback for Amazon's Starlink competitor, Project Kuiper, a United Launch Alliance (ULA) Vulcan rocket suffered its first mission failure in 20 years, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites on board. Ouch.

stories.headline: SNL skewers tech tycoons in a hilarious spycraft sketch
stories.summary: Saturday Night Live gathered all its impressions of the tech world's biggest names for a sketch about dating and spycraft. It was awkward, creepy, and a pretty funny take on the often-peculiar public personas of tech executives.

stories.headline: EPA's chemical-detecting plane is quietly grounded
stories.summary: This is a bit worrying: the EPA's crucial Cessna plane, designed to detect chemicals during disaster responses, is flying fewer missions and can no longer provide real-time data. This comes as toxic emergencies are actually on the rise, leaving a gap in our rapid response capabilities.

stories.headline: Astronomers finally weigh our home galaxy, the Milky Way
stories.summary: After years of cosmic guesswork, astronomers have at long last measured the mass of the Milky Way! This is a huge scientific achievement that helps us better understand our place in the universe and how galaxies evolve.

stories.headline: Forget just hours: the real sleep metric is deeper
stories.summary: Good news for those who stress about hitting exactly eight hours! New research suggests that simply clocking hours isn't the most important sleep metric. It's more about consistency, quality, and your individual circadian rhythm. So, stop fixating on the clock and listen to your body.

stories.headline: Why Europe should embrace "going full bananas" economically
stories.summary: Here's a fun, quirky idea: Europe should stop being so modest about its economic corridors and give them imaginative names like the famous "Blue Banana." The insight? Powerful branding and a clear vision can unlock unseen potential and logistical connections across borders.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang drama fuels fears of an AI bubble burst
stories.summary: The tech world is buzzing with the fallout from former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and alleged spy scandal. This whole saga is adding explosive new risk to the already-strained AI boom, raising concerns that a financial bubble might be ready to pop, even if the tech itself is brilliant.

stories.headline: US Senator slams Commerce Secretary over Nvidia chip sales to China
stories.summary: Senator Maria Cantwell is *not* happy. She's called out Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for apparently neglecting to enforce protections meant to keep Nvidia's coveted AI chips out of China. The worry is these chips are still finding their way to Beijing.

stories.headline: Apple dives into AI health with a new study app
stories.summary: Apple is pushing deeper into health tech, launching a new app for a study aimed at understanding how people actually use conversational AI health tools and how effective their responses truly are. They're trying to figure out if these bots are actually helpful, or just... bots.

stories.headline: Nvidia's security team under fire amid CEO scandal
stories.summary: As the drama around Jensen Huang unfolds, questions are mounting about Nvidia's internal security. The company's security chief quietly left in August, and with allegations of Huang's relationships potentially funneling chips to China, many are wondering: where was Nvidia's security team?

stories.headline: Indian startup Bharat Semi raises $24M for AI sensors
stories.summary: India is stepping up its AI game! Bharat Semi, an Indian chip startup, has secured a $24 million seed round. They're developing AI-enabled sensor technology, eyeing a significant slice of the rapidly growing global AI sensor market.
